To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have created a grasping database for human subjects for activities in daily living.
we collected a grasping database with depth, color, and kinematic data from 10 human subjects for activities-of-daily-living in unstructured environments.
we have developed a novel database of human grasping for activities of daily-living with depth, color, and kinematic data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
collecting and sharing a human grasping database with three different data streams.
the development of a grasping database with depth, color, and kinematic data for activities of daily life (ADLs).
the development of a human grasping database for daily activities of living with multiple sensor streams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper introduces a new grasping database for ADL with multiple sensing modalities, and it can be used for the development of new machine learning and big data techniques for grasping.
we provide a large scale database of grasps for activities of daily livings collected from multiple human users in unstructured environments.
this is a novel database that can serve the community as a benchmark for grasping analysis and recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present the first grasping database that includes color, depth and kinematic data for human grasps in unstructured environments.
we have collected the data, annotated the data, provided the tools for the data and made the data publicly available.
we have developed a new database with a hierarchical taxonomy of human grasps, and we have developed an open-source tool for data collection and annotation of grasping data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we provide a rich and diverse data set of human grasping in activities of daily living for research purposes in the robotics and machine learning communities.
the use of different sensing modalities and the use of a hierarchical grasp taxonomy is essential in developing machine learning techniques for human grasping and manipulation.
the use of different sensing modalities can provide rich information for grasping and manipulating objects in the real world.
